title: The 17 October Riots and the Struggle for Living Costs

beats.text: The 17 October riots saw nationwide unrest across France, Belgium, Italy, and Albania in 2026.
In mid-September, the Yellow vests movement saw a resurgence on social media as a starting point.
Students and school staff joined the protests due to poor school conditions and rising living costs.
Organisers reported between 550,000 and 800,000 people marched as violence spread across many French cities.
Rioters looted shops and set fires, causing hundreds of millions of euros in damage to public buildings.
Italian government plans included deploying 500 army troops to defend Milan on 19 October.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez submitted his resignation on 19 October, but President Macron rejected it.
Authorities implemented a curfew in several cities as the situation remains a focus for police.
Follow Orbitwire for the stories the whole world is talking about.

facts.evidence: In Limoges, the historic Hôtel de Ville was set ablaze during the evening; the fire continued into the following morning and partially destroyed the 19th-century building.

## Italy
The Italian government intended to deploy 500 army troops to defend Milan on 19 October and implement new security measures for 20 October, such as extending preventive detention for minors and cracking down on youth gangs.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 110 marches drew 550,000 participants, including 110,000 in Paris; organisers estimated 800,000.
